sources.name: Unicode Standard Annex #9: Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm

provenance.notes: Inputs are written by hand. Every level and visual order is computed by tools/extract/rules/lib/uax9.mjs with the bidi properties of UCD 18.0.0; that implementation passes all 770,241 cases of BidiTest.txt and all 91,707 cases of BidiCharacterTest.txt of the same version (tools/extract/rules/uax9-conformance.mjs). Which substrings count as islands, and therefore which rendering is "intended", is the researcher's judgment and needs review; the computed orders do not.

data.purpose: The classic shapes of mixed Arabic/Latin text, each with its logical string and the visual order the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm produces for it: once as a bare string ("plain") and once with every opposite-direction unit wrapped in a directional isolate ("isolated"). Where the two differ, the bare string is displayed wrongly and the case is the proof that isolation is required. Use it to test a bidi implementation (levels and order), an isolation helper (which ranges to wrap), and rendering (the order of characters on screen).

data.inputShape: { text: logical string without control characters; codePoints: the same string, one "U+XXXX" per code point; paragraphDirection: rtl | ltr | auto (first strong, UAX #9 P2–P3); islands?: [{ text, from, to, direction }] — code-point ranges [from, to) that are one opposite-direction unit }
data.expectedShape: plain: result for the bare string. isolated: result when each island is wrapped in LRI…PDI (direction ltr) or RLI…PDI (rtl) — the same as <bdi dir> or unicode-bidi: isolate — reported for the original characters only. Each result = { paragraphLevel, levels: resolved embedding level per code point, visualOrder: code-point indexes from the left edge to the right edge of the line, visualRuns: the line from left to right as [{ text: logical substring, from, to, direction }] where direction rtl means the run's characters are drawn right to left, mirrored?: indexes drawn with a mirrored glyph (UAX #9 L4) }. plainMatchesIsolated: false means the bare string is misordered. The whole line is assumed to fit on one line (L1/L2 applied once).

tagVocabulary.plain-is-wrong: isolating the islands changes the visual order: the bare string is a failure shape
tagVocabulary.plain-is-correct: the algorithm already orders the bare string as intended; isolation is harmless
tagVocabulary.no-island: nothing to isolate; the plain result is the expected rendering
tagVocabulary.first-strong: paragraph direction detected from the first strong character
